To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
pulmonary embolism is an uncommon complication of a traumatic pseudoaneurysmal arteriovenous malformation.
pulmonary embolism can originate from thrombosed pseudoaneurysms and arteriovenous malformations.
pulmonary embolism can occur from femoropoplitel pseudoaneurysms and arteriovenous shunts.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the rare case of massive pulmonary embolus secondary to femoropoplital pseudoaneurysmal arteriovenous shunt.
a rare case of massive pulmonary embolisation secondary to longstanding femoropoplitelal pseudoaneurism associated with arterio-venous fistula.
the case of a patient with a rare source of pulmonary emboli.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

a patient with massive pulmonary thromboembolism and a history of a traumatic femoropopoliteal pseudoaneuysm should undergo a complete evaluation of the lower extremity vessels to rule out the presence of a pseudoaneurysmal or arteriovenous shunt.
in the case of massive pulmonary embolus, it is necessary to search for its source, even when it seems to be obvious.

a patient who had a history of a bullet injury to his lower limb 7 years ago presented with a massive pulmonary embolus and the source of emboli was found to be a thrombosed pseudoaneurysmal sac and associated arteriovenous malformation.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
a long-standing traumatic pseudoaneurysma can be a source of massive pulmonary embolization, which should be considered in patients with pulmonary embolism.
a thorough clinical evaluation of the source of emboli should be done in every patient with massive pulmonary thromboembolism.
a traumatic pseudoaneurysmal arteriovenous shunt can be a rare cause of massive pulmonary embolization.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a history of traumatic injury should always raise a suspicion of pseudoaneurysms and arteriovenous malformations.
in the presence of longstanding traumatic arteriovenous pseudoaneurysms, a high index of suspicion for the possibility of pulmonary embolism should be maintained.
in patients with pulmonary embolism, especially in those with massive pulmonary emboli, a thorough search for potential sources of emboli should be performed.
